1.author: St. John Chrysostom
1.work: Homilies on the Gospel of St. John, Homily 2
1.text: What sayest thou, O blessed John? wishing to speak of the Father, didst thou make mention of the Son? Why dost thou not tell us of the Father first? Because, he replies, He could not be made known to us unless made known by His Son. 'No man hath seen God at any time; the only-begotten Son, which is in the bosom of the Father, He hath declared Him.' Therefore I lead you straight to His Son, that you may learn through Him concerning the Father. 'In the beginning was the Word.' What sayest thou? The Word was. As also concerning the Father he saith, 'God is.' Even so here, 'In the beginning was the Word.'

1.author: St. Augustine
1.work: Tractates on the Gospel of John, Tractate 1
1.text: What does 'In the beginning was the Word' mean? A house also is said in a similar way to be in the heart of the builder. The builder bears the house in his art; if he did not bear it in his art, how could he produce it by building? But the house which is in art is not the house which appears to our eyes. It exists invisibly in art, it will exist visibly in fabric. Behold, it is made; has it ceased to exist in art? The thing made in fabric is one thing, that which exists in art is another; the house abides in art.

14.author: St. Cyril of Alexandria
14.work: Commentary on the Gospel of John, Book 1
14.text: 'And the Word became flesh.' He did not change His own nature, but truly became Man, being God by nature, and putting on the flesh of man. He took to Himself what He was not, remaining what He was. For the Word, being God, became Man without ceasing to be God; that, in becoming Man, He might raise our nature with Himself.
